# agentic-report

Local living documents: `serve` hosts a loopback reader attached to its existing author Codex session;
`--agent standalone` explicitly starts a separate agent. Sources update as the author edits them.
Questions open beside selected passages; formatted replies, ordered cancellable waiting questions and
reader width/theme/change controls share the chat panel.
The same-author terminal messages and agent replies appear in a bounded ordered text history; correlated
browser questions appear once and mirrored input is never sent again.
Setup, flags, persistence and recovery: [Live operating guide](skills/agentic-report/references/process.md#live-local-document).

> Local declarative compiler for polished interactive HTML pages authored by agents.

Install the ready-made agent skill with:

    npx skills add witqq/agentic-report --skill agentic-report

Use it for static agent-to-human handoffs where evidence, relationships, code explanations, timelines,
visualizations, selected-text notes, or fragment-level review are clearer as a page than as a long chat
response. A custom skill may own domain research and call the pinned agentic-report CLI as its final rendering
stage. With `review: true` in the frontmatter, select eligible text and choose **Create note**; an anchored popover owns the
complete discussion and saved open/resolved ranges remain highlighted. **Review** is only a non-reflowing
list/import/export overlay. Review Workspace exports every selected-text note and compatible imported
whole-block thread together in one local `review.json`.

The section grammar composes arrangements, viewport rhythm, typography, local media framing, decorative
surfaces, bounded motion, and responsive action placement from closed attributes, without author CSS or
JavaScript. Reduced motion keeps all content visible. On narrow screens complex arrangements return to source
order, gallery scroll stays local, and the topbar uses accessible icon controls without widening the document.
Start with the neutral default theme and a section recipe; recipes include coordinated motion, so override
only the role you need. The built-in themes, layouts, recipes, directives, and commands are listed in the
generated catalog below; every attribute value is in the source contract. Authored operation labels stay
visible beside package icons on phones, and composition width remains separate from paragraph reading width.

Sources may embed maintained English and Russian Markdown variants with `localizations`. The generated page
selects an available system language, falls back to the primary entry, and shows a language selector only
when both variants exist. Switching replaces the complete page and keeps review/response state isolated by
locale. Single-language review export is version 3; multilingual export is version 4 with `report.locale`.

Requires Node.js 24.18.0 or newer. The first npx run requires npm registry access. Start with:

    npx --yes agentic-report@0.21.0 init ./my-page --starter landing --json
    npx --yes agentic-report@0.21.0 build ./my-page --output ./my-page.html --json

Edit `my-page/report.md` between the two commands and open `my-page.html` through `file://`. Build validates
the complete source before publishing. Use `validate` for separate diagnostics, `inspect` for source/catalog
discovery, and `fix` only for exact compiler-provided replacements.

Generated reports include a bottom Made with Agentic Report link by default. Set root metadata
`attribution: false` only when an unbranded artifact is explicitly required.

Agent JSON/NDJSON is the CLI default; use `--human` for prose or indented reference JSON. One directive
failure includes all independent violations in `related`, and `fix` applies only exact computed repairs.
